area: Spikes S9, S10 and S11: trust state through a schema read, constraint validation after the post-deploy script, system-named constraints through a publish to a copy
summary: Nothing in the tree answers S9, S10 or S11 yet. The spikes table at V3_MILESTONES.md:431-433 sends each answer to "the case's receipt in the catalog", and that catalog is still under archive/. The closest test is SpikeTests.cs:120-140 (Fact 11, a key's trust right after it is added, on 170.5.96 only). v3 reads a database's schema in one place, DacFx.Extract (io/DacFx.cs:99-109). V3_MILESTONES.md:307 already plans for constraint trust to be read from the catalog through SqlServer.Measure. I ran all three spikes in scratch against dbchange-sql, on DacFx 170.5.96 and 162.5.57 in-process, using golden-project packages built with the copied tool folder. The two releases agree on every point. S9: Extract and LoadFromDatabase keep both states. Disabled is the public property CheckConstraint.Disabled / ForeignKeyConstraint.Disabled (IsDisabled in model.xml). Untrusted is kept only as the internal annotation IsNotTrustedPropertyAnnotation, with no public property. A publish of the extracted package reproduces both states exactly. But no plan ever sees an untrusted key and no publish ever re-trusts it, a project cannot declare a key untrusted (build warning SQL70588), and v3 builds its base from the repository, so v3's trust step needs witnesses read from the catalog. S10: on both releases, with or without transactional scripts, validation (`PRINT 'Checking existing data…'` and then `WITH CHECK CHECK`) runs after the COMMIT and after the whole post-deploy script. A parent added by the seed therefore satisfies a new key. A 547 there leaves the main script and the seed applied and the key untrusted. S11: SQL Server names a system-named constraint after its object id, so names differ between the copy and an environment that has history. Extract does not keep the names either. Even so, the head plans against the copy and against the environment have equal operations, and their scripts are equal once each system name is replaced by its role. Two hazards came up along the way: a DF__-shaped name given explicitly (is_system_named = 0) is dropped by every plan, and any check written with IN, named or not, is dropped and re-created by every plan against the database it was published to. Scout evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/scout/s9-s11/ (probe/Probe.cs; s9-170.txt, s9-162.txt, s9g-170.txt, s9g-162.txt, s9-extracted-model.xml, s9-extracted-into-empty-170.sql, s10b-170.txt, s10c-170.txt, s10c-162.txt, s10-170-True-b-s10.sql, s11-170.txt, s11-162.txt, s11b-170.txt, s11b-162.txt). Every scout database was dropped afterwards.

items.name: S9 receipts on DacFx 170.5.96, in process: a schema read keeps a disabled check and an untrusted key, a publish of it reproduces both, and no plan sees the untrusted one
items.evidence: No test reads is_disabled or is_not_trusted except tests/Io.Tests/SpikeTests.cs:122-140 (Fact 11: trust after adding a key). v3's schema read is DacFx.Extract (io/DacFx.cs:99-109), under DacFx.Extraction (io/DacFx.cs:55-81). The element reader keeps only ModelTypeClass.Properties (io/Ssdt.cs:670-692). Test primitives: SqlServerFixture.RegisterAsync/ExecuteAsync/ScalarAsync (tests/Io.Tests/SqlServerFixture.cs:46-71; ScalarAsync binds @name), GoldenProject.Built/Pipeline/Publish (tests/Io.Tests/GoldenProject.Io.cs:35,47,53), ReadOnlyPrincipal.CreateAsync (tests/Io.Tests/ReadOnlyPrincipal.cs:41-67), and io's extract over a registered database: tests/Io.Tests/ModelElementsTests.cs:650 `DacFx.Extract(new SqlServer.Copy(Ok(CopyName.Of("the registered database", database.Name)), await SqlServerFixture.ServerAsync(), Repository.Root))`. Measured (s9g-170.txt and s9g-162.txt are identical). On the golden base I added FK_Order_Customer_CustomerId WITH NOCHECK over the seed's orphan (Order 4 → Customer 999), giving (disabled, not_trusted) = (0,1), and added CK_Product_Code then ran NOCHECK CONSTRAINT on it, giving (1,1). LoadFromDatabase reports CK Disabled=True and FK Disabled=False. The public static members of ForeignKeyConstraint are TypeClass, Disabled, NotForReplication, DeleteAction, UpdateAction, Host, Columns, ForeignColumns and ForeignTable; none is about trust, on either release. In model.xml the CK element carries `<Property Name="IsDisabled" Value="True"/>`, and both elements carry `<Annotation Type="IsNotTrustedPropertyAnnotation" />`. A publish of the extracted package to an empty database gives (1,1) and (0,1) again; its script uses `WITH NOCHECK ADD`, then `NOCHECK CONSTRAINT` for the disabled one and `WITH NOCHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT` for the untrusted one (s9-extracted-into-empty-170.sql:189-194, :337-341). I scripted the head add-a-foreign-key + add-a-check-constraint against that environment, live and package to package (DacServices.Script(source, target)). The operations are exactly Drop [dbo].[CK_Product_Code] and Create [dbo].[CK_Product_Code] (DROP, WITH NOCHECK ADD, WITH CHECK CHECK), with nothing for the untrusted key. After a Strict publish of that head the check is (0,0) and the key is still (0,1). With IgnoreWithNocheckOnForeignKeys and IgnoreWithNocheckOnCheckConstraints true, the plan is empty even for the disabled check (s9-170.txt). In a classic build of the golden project, `ALTER TABLE … WITH NOCHECK ADD CONSTRAINT` gives Build warning SQL70588 and no annotation, while `ALTER TABLE … NOCHECK CONSTRAINT` builds into IsDisabled=True.

It needs no class fixture, because GoldenProject.Built caches each head for the run. Every test carries [Trait("Category", "fixture")] and uses `using static DbChange.Tests.Expect;`.

Shared helpers:
(a) `const string Untrusted = "ALTER TABLE dbo.[Order] WITH NOCHECK ADD CONSTRAINT FK_Order_Customer_CustomerId FOREIGN KEY (CustomerId) REFERENCES dbo.Customer (Id);"`. This is the key of sample change add-a-foreign-key over the seed's orphan, as a failed deploy of that change leaves it.
(b) `const string Disabled = "ALTER TABLE dbo.Product ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Product_Code CHECK (LEN(Code) > 0); ALTER TABLE dbo.Product NOCHECK CONSTRAINT CK_Product_Code;"`. This is the check of add-a-check-constraint, then disabled.

(d) `static Task<int> Trust(string cs, string constraint) => SqlServerFixture.ScalarAsync(cs, "SELECT CAST(is_disabled AS int) * 2 + CAST(is_not_trusted AS int) FROM (SELECT name, is_disabled, is_not_trusted FROM sys.foreign_keys UNION ALL SELECT name, is_disabled, is_not_trusted FROM sys.check_constraints) c WHERE name = @name;", constraint)`. It returns 0 for trusted, 1 for untrusted and 3 for disabled.
(e) `static XElement ModelElement(string dacpac, string name)`: open model.xml with ZipFile and return the Element whose Name attribute is `name` (namespace http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/dac/Serialization/2012/02).
(f) `static List<(string Operation, string Item)> Operations(string report)`: the DeployReport namespace as in SpikeTests.cs:26.

items.name: S10 receipts on DacFx 170.5.96: constraint validation runs after the post-deploy script; the residue of a 547 there
items.evidence:
The golden base seed already holds the orphan Order 4 → Customer 999 (tests/Golden/project/Data/Seed.sql, Order MERGE). add-a-foreign-key (tests/Golden/changes/add-a-foreign-key/edits.txt) declares FK_Order_Customer_CustomerId. Measured in s10-170-True-b-s10.sql (the head's plan against the published base, under the pipeline profile). Each marker occurs once, in this order:
- `WITH NOCHECK` ADD of the key at line 154
- `PRINT N'The transacted portion of the database update succeeded.'` at 183
- `COMMIT TRANSACTION` at 184
- the post-deploy header `the POST-DEPLOY slot` at 192
- the seed row `(999, N'Wayne` at 322
- `Post-deploy complete` at 501
- `Checking existing data against newly created constraints` at 505
- `WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT [FK_Order_Customer_CustomerId]` at 513
The head publishes, and the key lands trusted (0,0). Without the seed edit (add-a-foreign-key alone) the publish fails at Msg 547 (SQL72014 and SQL72045), leaving the key (0,1). With a second orphan the seed does not fix (Order 5 → 998), the publish fails at Msg 547 after Customer 999 was inserted, and the key is left (0,1). That is: main applied, post-deploy applied, validation failed. All of this holds on 162.5.57 and under DacFx's default options (IncludeTransactionalScripts False: same order, no COMMIT) (s10c-170.txt, s10c-162.txt). The publish-failure pattern through io is at tests/Io.Tests/CopyTests.cs:181-200: copy.Publish returns Failed with code server.failed and a message starting "copy:<name> failed the statement: Msg N: ".

items.name: S11 receipts on DacFx 170.5.96: system-named constraints through a publish to a copy, and the head plans against the copy and the environment
items.evidence:
add-unnamed-constraints (tests/Golden/changes/add-unnamed-constraints/edits.txt) creates dbo.Note with unnamed PK, FK, UNIQUE, two DEFAULTs (Body N'', Pinned 0) and three CHECKs. ModelElementsTests.cs:522-540 already shows that v3 keys unnamed constraints by their target (`DefaultConstraint [dbo].[Note].[Pinned].[TargetColumn]`), not by name. Measured (s11-170.txt; s11-162.txt identical apart from random PK__/UQ__ suffixes):
- DF__, CK__ and FK__ suffixes are the object id in hex. Two fresh databases published from one package therefore get the same DF/CK/FK names, while PK__/UQ__ names differ.
- After the environment was given history (two tables created and dropped before the publish), every system name differed between the environment and the copy, e.g. DF__Note__Body__4F7CD00D against DF__Note__Body__49C3F6B7.
- Script(head, env) and Script(head, copy), where the head changes Body's default to N'-', had equal operations (Drop unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note] ×2; Create Default Constraint: unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note]; Create Check Constraint: unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note]). Each script DROPs the database's own name. The scripts are equal once the database name and each system name are replaced by its role.
- Extract(env) published to a fresh database kept none of the names: the two Score checks even swapped names.
- sp_rename to `DF__Note__Body__0BADF0nn` sets is_system_named = 0. After that, Script(the base, env) drops every such explicit name and creates an unnamed constraint in its place (12 operations).
items.remaining:
New sample change tests/Golden/changes/change-an-unnamed-default/edits.txt. It copies add-unnamed-constraints/edits.txt (the Note table and the NoteCount procedure) with `Body NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT (N'')` changed to `DEFAULT (N'-')`, so it applies on its own to the base and differs from add-unnamed-constraints only in Body's default. Shared helpers: `static async Task<string> Name(string cs, string sql)`, an ExecuteScalar string read of about 6 lines (SqlServerFixture only returns ints); and `static string Normalized(string script, string database) => Regex.Replace(script.Replace(database, "<database>", StringComparison.Ordinal), @"\[((?:DF|CK|FK|UQ|PK)__[^\]]*__)[0-9A-F]{8,16}\]", "[$1<id>]")`. The Body default's name: `SELECT name FROM sys.default_constraints WHERE parent_object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.Note') AND COL_NAME(parent_object_id, parent_column_id) = N'Body'`.

- env = RegisterAsync. First give it history: ExecuteAsync("CREATE TABLE dbo.History (A INT NOT NULL DEFAULT (0), B INT NULL CHECK (B > 0)); CREATE TABLE dbo.History2 (A INT NOT NULL DEFAULT (0)); DROP TABLE dbo.History; DROP TABLE dbo.History2;"). A comment must say why: two fresh databases get the same object ids, so the same DF/CK/FK names.

- Assert both Body names start "DF__Note__Body__" and differ, and is_system_named = 1 on both.
- Plan(head = Built(Change("change-an-unnamed-default"))) against each: Operations equal; env's script contains "DROP CONSTRAINT [" + envName + "]"; Normalized(envScript, env.Name) == Normalized(copyScript, copy.Name).

Test D2: env with history as in D1, base published. DacServices.Extract into a ScratchFolder.Temporary file, published to fresh. fresh's Body name differs from env's and is_system_named = 1: names are SQL Server's, not the model's.

items.name: Found while running S11: a check written with IN is dropped and re-created by every plan against the database it was published to
items.evidence: The plan of add-unnamed-constraints against a copy just published from it is not empty. It is Drop unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note]; Create Check Constraint: unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note], with script `DROP CONSTRAINT [CK__Note__Pinned__…]` and `ADD CHECK (Pinned IN (0, 1))`. SQL Server stores the check as `([Pinned]=(1) OR [Pinned]=(0))`. A named check behaves the same: in an in-memory package, `CONSTRAINT CK_T_A_In CHECK (A IN (0, 1))` gives Drop/Create [dbo].[CK_T_A_In]. `CHECK (C = 1 OR C = 0)` and `CHECK ([C]=(0) OR [C]=(1))` give no operation. ScriptNewConstraintValidation=false changes nothing. Identical on 162.5.57 and 170.5.96 (s11b-170.txt, s11b-162.txt). The golden base has no IN check, which is why law 2′'s and M1.3's drift tests are green today. ModelElementsTests.cs:536-537 already records that the Pinned check's Expression differs between package and database.
items.remaining: Test E1 in SpikeReceiptTests: copy = RegisterAsync; Publish(Built(Change("add-unnamed-constraints"))). Plan the same package against the copy. Operations == [("Drop", "unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note]"), ("Create", "Check Constraint: unnamed constraint on [dbo].[Note]")], and the script contains "ADD CHECK (Pinned IN (0, 1))". Its plan is Drop/Create [dbo].[CK_T_A_In]. Then record the consequence where the operator decides (see question) and in NEXT.md.

items.question: Every plan against a database holding a check written with IN (named or unnamed) drops and re-creates it, on both DacFx releases. That means `check drift` (law 2′, M1.3) reports drift on that environment forever, and WP 3.5's identity step (the plan from the base to the copy is empty) fails for any such project, the golden add-unnamed-constraints head included. Should v3 (a) treat it as an author rule in knowledge/, write such checks as the OR form SQL Server stores, and keep drift strict, or (b) teach drift and identity to read a Drop and Create of one check whose two expressions match once parsed as no difference?

A schema read keeps both states, but v3's base is built from the repository, which cannot declare untrusted (SQL70588), and no plan or publish touches an untrusted key. So WP 3.5's step 4 reads is_disabled and is_not_trusted for the touched constraints through SqlServer.Measure: an allowlisted `SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.foreign_keys WHERE parent_object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'<schema>.<table>') AND name = N'<key>' AND is_not_trusted = 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END`, which yields integers only, as :307 plans. It restores a disabled constraint with `NOCHECK CONSTRAINT` and an untrusted one with `WITH NOCHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT`, exactly as DacFx's own publish of an extracted package does. A disabled constraint changes the head plan (re-enable on every deploy), so it must be reproduced before planning, not only around planting.
(4) V3_MILESTONES.md:917-918: S10 found the same order on 162.5.57 and under default options, so a lookup seeded post-deploy satisfies a new key on both releases.

risks: S2 may run a probe for each sample change in tests/Golden/changes/ ('for each sample change', V3_MILESTONES.md:428). If it enumerates GoldenProject.SampleChanges, the two new folders (add-a-foreign-key-whose-parent-the-seed-adds, change-an-unnamed-default) join its set and change its golden files under tests/Golden/data-loss-checks/. The two work packages must agree on who adds them, and in what order.

The 162.x half depends on S2's route. A VersionOverride of Microsoft.SqlServer.DacFx contradicts the 'One version per package' comment at Directory.Packages.props:2 and needs a DECISIONS.md line. The 162 program must be restored and built before the outbound-denied job's deny step, which happens if it sits in DbChange.sln. 162.5.57 pulls Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 5.1.6 and Azure.Identity 1.11.4 into that program only. NuGet audit raised no warning for them here, but a new advisory would fail the build under warnings as errors.

S9's receipt pins the internal model.xml annotation name IsNotTrustedPropertyAnnotation. That is not a public contract, so a DacFx bump may rename it. The test then fails loudly, which is intended: a receipt is re-run on every pin bump, as INV-H6-01 asks.

S11 measured without history gives a false 'names kept': two fresh databases get the same object ids, and DF__/CK__/FK__ names end in the object id in hex. The environment database must be given history (objects created and dropped) before its publish, and the test must say why in a comment.

The IN-list re-create breaks law 2′ (check drift) and WP 3.5's identity step on any project that writes CHECK (... IN (...)). It is the same on both releases and invisible today only because the golden base has no IN check. The operator should decide before WP 3.5's identity step or the first real `check drift` against Dev.

S9's plan-visibility half is relative to the golden profile. With IgnoreWithNocheckOnForeignKeys and IgnoreWithNocheckOnCheckConstraints set true, even a disabled constraint leaves the plan. S7's captured Octopus profile decides which holds in the environments.

An environment's DF__-shaped names given explicitly (is_system_named = 0, e.g. a schema scripted by SSMS, or a renamed constraint) make the environment's plan differ from the copy's: every plan drops them. The copy cannot reproduce this, but `check drift` against the environment shows it as drift, so R12's drift-on-every-result covers it.

Run time: the receipts publish the golden base about ten times (the S11 env, copy, extract copy and renamed env; S10's two copies; S9's env and fresh copy; E1). On the fixture lane that adds roughly one to two minutes on Ubuntu and more on Windows LocalDB. The read-only principal needs SQL logins, which SpikeTests already relies on in both lanes.
